title: "Blues in the Night" with Lunceford at the Casa Manana
summary: His first film was Warner Brothers' "Blues in the Night" filmed while the band played the Casa Manana in Culver City.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: But those were the ones I did with him over there. Of course, the first movie I did was with Lincelford in about '38, and this was that "Blues in the Night" movie with Jack -- what's his name? Was it Jack Carson? I think it was Jack Carson. It's way back.
I've seen references to it, but I don't really know. It was a feature-length movie, right?
Blues in the Night, yeah, we did it for Warner Brothers. I remember that. And we were playing at the Casa Manana same time we did it, about '39, I think. It's way back, long time ago.
It was a full length feature movie?

Yeah. Well, we only had one little spot in there, you know, very short, and that was written in. I tell you how that -- we got that spot -- was Ray Heindorf -- he did all the musical things out there at -- a lot of them anyway at Warner Brothers back there then. And he used to come in there every night to hear us, and he liked the band and this old Casa Manana, you know, and Frank Sebastian -- Frank Sebastian's Cotton Club. Then he changed it to Casa Manana in later years, out in Culver City.

And we did quite a lot of -- quite a lot of business out there when we played this room. We would stay in there about two or three weeks whenever we came in. It was a long run for us, you know. But we made the movie the same time we were out there. I remember that. We only worked on it about two days, something like that, because we just had that one spot.
